findings.text: The spec requires "Record the probe in `launcher.json`: `probe: {args, ok}`." This assignment is the only place `args.probe` reaches a launcher record, in the one-shot `launch()`; the `--rounds N` path builds its own `launcher` in `repairLoop` (internal/core/run/repair.go:77-86) without `Probe: args.probe`. A multi-round launch with a probing agent therefore runs the probe but leaves no `probe` key in launcher.json, and the new eval and probe tests only exercise the one-shot path. Verified with a temporary test: a passing probe with RoundsRaw=2 produced launcher.json with no `probe` field.

This `neovate` row omits the boolean `-q`/`--quiet` that makes the CLI non-interactive. The cited vendor help says "Run the code agent with a prompt, interactive by default, use -q/--quiet for non-interactive mode", and RESEARCH-2's headless invocation is `neovate -q "<prompt>"` with the prompt as a trailing positional. `verdict run --agent neovate` therefore composes `neovate --model M --x <directive>` and starts an interactive TUI instead of a headless agent, so the review artifact is never written and the run ends as a timeout or no-artifact refusal. The new argv and --print tests assert the same missing flag, so they cannot catch it.

This `qoder` row omits the boolean `-p`/`--print` that enters headless mode. The cited vendor doc says "To enter Headless mode, add the `--print` flag (short form `-p`)" and lists the invocation as `qoder -p "<prompt>"` with a trailing positional prompt. The composed argv is `qoder --model M --x <directive>`, which launches the interactive CLI rather than the headless one; no review artifact follows and the run times out or refuses no-review-artifact. The row's argv and --print tests pin the same wrong argv.

This `qodercn` row omits the boolean `-p`/`--print` that enters headless mode. The cited vendor doc says "Enter Headless mode by adding `--print` (short form `-p`)" and shows `qodercn -p "<prompt>"` with a trailing positional prompt. The composed argv is `qodercn --model M --x <directive>`, so the launch opens the interactive CLI instead of writing the review, ending in a timeout or no-review-artifact refusal. The row's argv and --print tests repeat the same omission.

This `kode` row omits the boolean `-p`/`--print` that selects non-interactive output. The cited vendor parser describes the program as "starts an interactive session by default, use -p/--print for non-interactive output", and RESEARCH-2's headless invocation is `kode -p "<prompt>"` with a trailing positional prompt. The composed argv `kode --model M --x <directive>` starts an interactive session, so a launch cannot produce the review artifact. The new table-driven argv and --print tests enshrine the same missing flag.
